questions.stem: What is the difference between a view and a materialized view?

options.text: A view runs its query each time it's read; a materialized view stores precomputed results and refreshes them
A view stores data; a materialized view doesn't
A materialized view can't be queried with SQL

questions.explanation: Materialized views keep results stored and are refreshed, so reads are fast; views are just saved queries.

questions.stem: Which object incrementally processes append-only data as it arrives, such as new files?
questions.explanation: Streaming tables are designed for append-only sources and process each input only once.

questions.stem: A dashboard reads a costly aggregation over large silver tables many times a day. Which gold object fits?

options.text: A materialized view of the aggregation

questions.explanation: A materialized view stores the result, so every dashboard read doesn't recompute it.

questions.stem: Which SQL creates a materialized view?

options.text: CREATE VIEW sales_by_day MATERIALIZE AS SELECT ...
CREATE CACHED VIEW sales_by_day AS SELECT ...
CREATE MATERIALIZED VIEW sales_by_day AS SELECT ...

questions.explanation: CREATE MATERIALIZED VIEW defines a materialized view.

questions.stem: When is a plain view a better gold object than a materialized view?

options.text: When the query is cheap or must always reflect the latest data at read time
When the query is very expensive and read often

questions.explanation: Views compute results on demand, so they're always current; materialized views pay off for expensive or frequently used queries.
